facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 火_比肩 (Fire carrying The Twin). Persona The Twin (比肩). Definition line: "Same nature, same register, the standard you hold yourself to". Keyword Independence, charge steady, poles catalyst Self-trust / friction Isolation. Family function: Body. Cost dimension: the standard held to oneself; company that truly matches is rare. Arena: mirrors, stride, equal measure, walking beside. Classical portrait: same nature, same register; the standard held to oneself; self-reliance that can wall others out. Ruled domains: Peers, Independence, Self-reliance. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 劫财.
Element arena: Fire (flame, light, warmth, fuel, the hearth, the blaze). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Warmth amplifying warmth — illumination running without containment".
- k2_overview: "Your Fire moves as the Twin: a flame that burns on its own fuel and stands level with every other light. You warm a gathering without needing to lead it, and you bristle when anyone tries to carry you. Two torches burn brighter side by side. That is your theory of company, and mostly it works."
- k2_functional: "Your energy burns bright and social: fed by activity, drained by standing in another’s shadow."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Self-lit","Vivid","Undimmed"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Peers":"Your peers are fellow fires: vivid friends, loud tables, mutual sparks. The heat of comparison can flare into rivalry fast, so choose companions who celebrate blaze rather than compete for oxygen.","Independence":"Fire independence is your own hearth: warmth that no one can dim by leaving. Build a life that stays lit in an empty house, and company becomes a pleasure instead of a fuel line.","Self-reliance":"You reignite yourself after setbacks that extinguish others, usually overnight. The skill to learn is banking coals: resting without calling it defeat, so the relight costs less each time."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 火_劫财 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Spark-chasing","Fearless","Electrifying"],"friction":["Hot-headed","Resentful","Explosive"]}
- Sibling cell 火_劫财 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "The fuse is short, dry, and pre-lit. The wrong word, the cut-off in traffic, the tone in an email: ignition beats deliberation to the scene every time. Afterward you cool fast and repair sincerely. The people nearby, though, have all learned the smell of smoke."

Core element Fire, energy element Fire. Law: Fire and Fire are the same element (the self pair). Relative to the core the energy is the self, so Fire is this core's Body. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Fire on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Fire as the Body is the Overfueled band's case (the core has more than it channels); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 火_火's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You go it alone by default, before anyone refuses to help. Waiting on help feels like being slowed, so you do it yourself rather than explain it to anyone. You finish sooner and carry the full weight with no one to share it.

value_b.text: Going it alone is your first answer to everything. You would have to ask for help and wait on it, while your own hands are already free, so you use your hands every time. Remember that you were not built to be the only pair.

value.text: Whenever a job splits two ways, you carry both ends alone. Holding it yourself matters more than keeping a peer in the loop, so you leave them nothing to carry. You keep your peers on the outside of work they wanted a share in.

value.text: Being told is the one thing you cannot take. Your own read feels more solid than any second opinion, so you hold it rather than test it. You carry a wrong read for weeks that one honest word from a peer would have fixed.

value_b.text: You would rather be wrong on your own terms than right on someone else's. You let no one tell you, because being told feels like handing over the one thing that is yours. Remember that you lose nothing by being told by a peer.

value.text: You wall people out without meaning to, by needing nothing from them. Matching you is rare, so you keep your own company rather than settle. You shut out the right ones as fast as the wrong ones, and that is worth remembering.

value_b.text: Your wall is up before anyone has knocked. Your own standard is the one you hold to, so you would rather stay unseen than be seen falling short of it. You built the wall for safety, remember, and it mostly keeps out company.

value.text: Walling people out keeps your standard safe and your evenings empty. You hold out for company that matches instead of company nearby, since near enough feels like settling. You go without closeness, and closeness only grows where someone sees you at less than your best.

value.text: You put the wall up highest when someone gets closest. Being seen fine from far matters more than being seen tired up close, so you hold a peer there. You leave them a friend they can see and never quite reach.
